G5A01: In a series LC circuit at resonance the two reactances cancel, leaving only resistance, so impedance is very low.
G5A02: Reactance is the opposition to AC caused by capacitance or inductance. Resistance is the DC-style opposition.
G5A03: An inductor opposes AC with reactance.
G5A04: A capacitor opposes AC with reactance too.
G5A05: Inductive reactance rises with frequency: XL = 2 pi f L.
G5A06: Capacitive reactance falls as frequency rises: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C).
G5A07: Admittance is the inverse of impedance (1/Z). Conductance is the inverse of resistance.
G5A08: Impedance = voltage divided by current (Z = E / I), like Ohm's law for AC.
G5A09: Reactance is an opposition to current, so it is measured in ohms.
G5A10: Transformers, pi-networks and lengths of transmission line can all match impedances at RF. All of these.
G5A11: Reactance is X (XL for inductors, XC for capacitors). Z is impedance.
G5A12: At resonance XL equals XC, and because they act in opposite directions they cancel.
G5B02: In parallel, the total current is the sum of the branch currents.
G5B04: P = E x I = 12 x 0.2 = 2.4 watts.
G5B05: P = I squared x R = 0.007 x 0.007 x 1,250 = 0.061 watts, about 61 milliwatts.
G5B06: 200 V peak-to-peak = 100 V peak. RMS = 100 x 0.707 = 70.7 V. PEP = 70.7 x 70.7 / 50 = 100 watts.
G5B07: RMS is defined as the AC value that heats a resistor the same as that much DC.
G5B08: Peak = 120 x 1.414 = 169.7 V. Peak-to-peak is twice that: 339.4 volts.
G5B10: 1 dB down leaves 10 to the power -0.1 = 0.794 of the power, so 1 - 0.794 = 20.6 percent is lost.
G5B11: An unmodulated carrier is steady, so its peak power equals its average power: ratio 1.00.
G5B12: E = square root of (P x R) = square root of (1200 x 50) = square root of 60,000 = 245 volts.
G5B13: Unmodulated carrier: PEP equals average power, so 1060 watts.
G5B14: 500 V peak-to-peak = 250 V peak. RMS = 250 x 0.707 = 176.8 V. PEP = 176.8 x 176.8 / 50 = 625 watts.
G5C01: The changing magnetic field of the primary links to the secondary: mutual inductance.
G5C02: Run backward, a 4:1 step-down becomes a 1:4 step-up, so the voltage is multiplied by 4.
G5C05: Stepping voltage up steps current down, so the primary carries more current and needs thicker wire.
G5C06: Turns ratio 1500 / 500 = 3, so 120 V x 3 = 360 volts.
G5C07: Turns ratio = square root of the impedance ratio = square root of (600 / 50) = square root of 12 = 3.5 to 1.
G5C08: Capacitors in parallel add: 5.0 + 5.0 + 0.75 nF (750 pF) = 10.750 nanofarads.
G5C09: Equal capacitors in series: divide by how many. 100 / 3 = 33.3 microfarads.
G5C10: Equal inductors in parallel: divide by how many. 10 / 3 = 3.3 millihenries.
G5C11: Inductors in series add, like resistors: 20 + 50 = 70 millihenries.
G5C12: Capacitors in series combine like parallel resistors: (20 x 50) / (20 + 50) = 1000 / 70 = 14.3 microfarads.
G5C13: Capacitors add in parallel, so add a capacitor in parallel to increase capacitance.
G5C14: Inductors add in series, so add an inductor in series to increase inductance.
G6A01: Don't discharge a 12 volt lead-acid battery below 10.5 volts if you want it to last.
G6A02: Low internal resistance means the battery can deliver high current.
G6A03: Germanium diodes turn on at about 0.3 volts.
G6A04: Electrolytics pack a lot of capacitance into a small size.
G6A05: Silicon diodes turn on at about 0.7 volts.
G6A06: A wire-wound resistor is a coil, so its inductance upsets RF circuits.
G6A07: As a switch, a transistor sits at saturation (fully on) or cutoff (fully off).
G6A08: Low voltage ceramic capacitors are cheap.
G6A09: In a MOSFET, a thin insulating layer separates the gate from the channel (metal-oxide).
G6A10: The control grid sits between cathode and plate and controls the flow of electrons.
G6A11: Above its self-resonant frequency, an inductor's stray capacitance takes over and it acts like a capacitor.
G6A12: The screen grid cuts the capacitance between the control grid and the plate.
G6B01: A ferrite's mix (the material blend) decides which frequencies it works best at.
G6B03: CMOS uses far less power than TTL.
G6B04: BNC connectors are good to about 4 GHz.
G6B05: Ferrite toroids give large inductance, can be tuned for a frequency range, and hold the field inside the core. All of these.
G6B06: An op amp is an analog device.
G6B07: Type N connectors are moisture resistant and good to 10 GHz.
G6B08: An LED lights when forward biased.
G6B10: A ferrite bead adds impedance in the path of common-mode current on the outside of the shield.
G6B11: SMA is a small threaded connector good to several GHz.
G6B12: RCA phono plugs are used for audio and low frequency or DC connections.
